t: In an alcove in the grounds of Guy's Hospital, you're looking at a statue of the poet John Keats. Sculptor Stuart Williamson made it, and it was unveiled in 2007. Keats belongs here because he trained as a doctor at this hospital. He is now remembered as one of the great Romantic poets. He died of tuberculosis at twenty-five, when his poems had been in print for less than four years. They were indifferently received in his lifetime, but his fame grew rapidly after his death.
